safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures denial of SOB, palpitations, headaches, and vision changes, but does not include denial of chest pain (part of the Gold fact).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the explicit denial of chest pain is primarily a documentation completeness issue; the encounter focus is abdominal/urinary symptoms and there is no suggestion of cardiopulmonary pathology requiring action. This omission is unlikely to change clinical decision-making in this context.

safety_verdicts.content: Lower abdominal pain with hematuria and urinary frequency
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold explicitly notes no frank hematuria; transcript is uncertain ('urine a little pink', 'can't say maybe' re blood). Labeling as 'hematuria' is not supported and contradicts Gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “hematuria” converts an uncertain/possible finding (“urine a little pink,” unsure about blood) into a definite red-flag symptom, which can drive unnecessary escalation (e.g., hematuria workup, imaging, referrals) and misframe the differential. While it is unlikely to directly cause severe injury, it can lead to avoidable tests and altered management priorities.
